overview: Two of the three main RNA types, playing very different roles in the translation process.
genZNote: mRNA carries the recipe. rRNA is part of the kitchen equipment that reads it.

aspects.label: Function
aspects.valueA: Carries the genetic code copied from DNA to the ribosome for protein synthesis.
aspects.valueB: Forms the structural and catalytic core of the ribosome itself.

aspects.label: Relative Abundance in Cell
aspects.valueB: Most abundant RNA type, making up the bulk of total cellular RNA.

aspects.label: Stability
aspects.valueA: Generally short-lived, quickly degraded after use.
aspects.valueB: Very stable, as it's a permanent structural part of the ribosome.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: rRNA makes up about 80% of total cellular RNA — a frequently tested numerical fact.
overlay.memoryTrick: mRNA = messenger, delivers the message once. rRNA = ribosomal, sticks around as the machine.
overlay.commonMisconception: rRNA doesn't carry genetic code for a specific protein — it's structural/catalytic, not an information carrier like mRNA.
